title: Grade 11 Biology National Exam & Practice 2016 (5 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 5 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: A mother milks her cow every morning and the milk usually forms curd after three days. What is the first step to investigate why this change happens?
options: Take action to prevent the milk from curdling
Read scientific articles about the reason for curdling of milk
Formulate hypothesis about the reason for milk curdling
Ask a question why the milk forms curd
questions.explanation:
The first step in a scientific investigation is to identify and ask a question about the observed phenomenon.
 In this case, the investigation begins by asking why the milk forms curd.

questions.questionText: A drug efficacy test was conducted under similar set up on two groups of infected mice (A and B). Group A were the control whereas group B were experimental group. A student gave a placebo to the control group and the drug to the experimental group. At the end, the experimental group got better. Which one of the following is true about the result?
questions.explanation: Since the control group received a placebo and did not improve while the experimental group received the drug and got better under the same conditions, the improvement can be attributed to the drug. Therefore, the drug has an effect.

questions.questionText: Suppose you did an experiment in a biology laboratory and need to report your work to your biology teacher. Which one of the following steps is correct to report the finding?
options: Title -> Procedure -> Result -> Hypothesis -> Prediction -> Evaluation
Title -> Hypothesis ->  Procedure -> Prediction -> Conclusion -> Result
Title -> Hypothesis -> Prediction -> Procedure -> Result -> Conclusion
Title -> Prediction -> Procedure -> Hypothesis -> Result -> Conclusion
questions.explanation: The correct order to report a scientific experiment is: start with the Title, state the Hypothesis, make a Prediction, describe the Procedure, present the Results, and end with the Conclusion.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives contains only organic molecules?
options: Glucose, carbon dioxide, glycine and linoleic acid
Methane, calcium carbonate, linoleic acid and glucose
Methane, glycine, linoleic acid and glucose
Linoleic acid, glucose, calcium carbonate and methane
questions.explanation:
Organic molecules contain carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds.

 Methane (CH4), glycine (an amino acid), linoleic acid (a fatty acid), and glucose (a carbohydrate) are all organic molecules. Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) and carbon dioxide (CO2) are inorganic.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following properties permits insects to freely walk on water? Its high
questions.explanation:
The ability of insects, such as water striders, to walk on water is due to the high surface tension of water.
 Surface tension is the cohesive force among water molecules at the surface that creates a film-like effect, resisting external force.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following organic molecules observes ester bonds in its molecular structure?
questions.explanation:
Triglycerides are fats composed of one glycerol molecule bonded to three fatty acids through ester bonds.
 Amino acids, glycogen, and cellulose do not contain ester bonds in their basic structures.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is correct about the structural organization of hemoglobin? It is formed
options: when a polypeptide chain folds itself during protein synthesis.
through the association of two or more polypeptide chains.
through folding of secondary structure of a polypeptide chain.
by hydrogen bonding between quaternary and tertiary structures.
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is a quaternary protein made of four polypeptide chains (two alpha and two beta chains) that associate together to form a functional protein capable of carrying oxygen.

questions.questionText: The presence of large amount of lipid reduces the density of an animal. Which function of triglycerides is related to this fact?
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are less dense than water, so storing large amounts of lipids helps animals, especially aquatic ones, maintain buoyancy and float more easily.

questions.questionText: The missing number represented by the letter " n " in the formula of maltose (C12H18O11) is
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements explains how the allosteric inhibitors act on enzymes? By binding to the
options: substrate and preventing it from binding to the active site
site other than the active site and altering the shape of the active site
active site of an enzyme and blocking the substrate
active site and altering the shape of the enzyme
questions.explanation:
Allosteric inhibitors bind to a site on the enzyme other than the active site (the allosteric site).
 This binding changes the shape of the enzyme, particularly the active site, preventing the substrate from binding effectively and thus reducing enzyme activity.

questions.questionText: Why are enzymes considered special molecules in metabolism? because
options: metabolic processes can produce special products in the presence of enzymes.
enzymes facilitate metabolic reactions under controlled physiological conditions.
enzymes are protein molecules that act as a source of energy.
reactions can't totally take place in the absence of enzymes.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up metabolic reactions without being consumed, allowing reactions to occur efficiently under normal physiological conditions of temperature and pH

questions.questionText: Which one of the following properties of enzymes shows their catalytic nature?
options: Being altered in a chemical reaction
Changing the nature of the product
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts because they speed up chemical reactions by lowering the activation energy required for the reaction to occur, without being consumed or altered in the process.

questions.questionText: If an enzyme is named as "EC 3.4.11.1" in a systematic naming, what does the number " 3 " represents?
options: sub-subclass of an enzyme in relation to its protein nature.
ultra-subclass of an enzyme that is related to the place where they act.
sub-class of an enzyme in relation to the source from where it was discovered.
main class of an enzyme which indicates the type of reaction it catalyses.
questions.explanation:
In the Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering system, the first number represents the main class of the enzyme, indicating the type of chemical reaction it catalyzes.

 For example, '3' denotes hydrolases, which catalyze hydrolysis reactions.

questions.questionText: In the lock-and-key model of enzymatic action, the activation energy is lowered through
options: provision of alternative pathway for the reaction.
straining of the substrate molecules bound to the active site.
permanent modification of the active site of the enzyme.
questions.explanation:
In the lock-and-key model, the substrate fits precisely into the enzyme's active site.

 Binding strains certain chemical bonds in the substrate, making it easier for the reaction to occur and thereby lowering the activation energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following minerals are used as cofactor for the enzymed alcohol dehydrogenase?
questions.explanation:
Alcohol dehydrogenase requires zinc ions (Zn²⁺) as a cofactor. 
Zinc helps stabilize the enzyme structure and plays a key role in the catalytic activity during the oxidation of alcohols.

questions.questionText:
A student made an experiment to observe the effect of Temperature on catalase of mashed potato. After three parallel trials, he obtained the following results.
At which temperature was the reaction fastest?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: A student focused a slide of an onion epidermal cell on pre-estimated width of 2 millimeter field of view under a microscope. What will be the width of each individual cell if you count 8 cells that fit to the field of view during your observation?
questions.explanation: The width of a single cell is calculated by dividing the field of view by the number of cells: 2 mm ÷ 8 = 0.25 mm

questions.questionText: Which one of the following arrangement of molecules in the fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane is correct?
options: Phospholipids fill the protein like a sandwich to retain its rigidity.
Phospholipid molecules are peripherally attached to proteins.
Phospholipids are inserted into the bilayer of protein molecules.
Protein molecules are studded between the phospholipid bilayers.
questions.explanation: In the fluid mosaic model, the cell membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded (integral proteins) or attached (peripheral proteins). This arrangement allows fluidity and selective transport across the membrane.

questions.questionText: What is the role of cholesterol in the cell membrane? It
options: anchors integral proteins to the cytoskeleton.
reduce the fluidity of the cell membrane.
acts as receptor site for hormones and other signaling molecules.
transports hydrophilic molecules into the cell.
questions.explanation:
Cholesterol molecules are interspersed within the phospholipid bilayer of the cell membrane. 

They stabilize the membrane structure by reducing fluidity at high temperatures and preventing it from becoming too rigid at low temperatures.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following table on the function of cellular organelles:

Which numbers in the above table show the **correct function** of the given organelles?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Potato slices of equal weighed were immersed in four different concentrations of salt solutions. The solutions were **1.5, 1.0, 0.5, and 0.1 molars**. After a day, the potato slices were re-weighted. Which potato slice weighs the least? The one from
questions.explanation:
Potato cells lose water by osmosis when placed in a hypertonic solution (higher solute concentration than the cell sap).

 The 1.5 M salt solution is the most concentrated, so the potato slice in it loses the most water and therefore weighs the least.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the differences between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells? Prokaryotic cells have
options: membrane bound organelles whereas eukaryotic cells don't have it.
small ribosomes whereas eukaryotic cells have large ribosomes.
cell wall whereas eukaryotic cells don't have cell wall.
division of labor whereas eukaryotic cells don't have it.
questions.explanation:
Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes, which are smaller than the 80S ribosomes found in eukaryotic cells. 
Eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles and more complex internal structures, unlike prokaryotes.

questions.questionText: Which biological tool is correctly matched with its function?
options: Burette - to measure mass of a substance
Theodolite - to measure the rate of water flow
questions.explanation:
Petri dishes are shallow, flat-lidded dishes used to culture and grow microorganisms under controlled conditions.
 The other options are incorrectly matched with their functions.

questions.questionText: A student centrifuge a solution containing plant material in order to separate them based on their mass. After 10 minutes of centrifugation some of the components move to the bottom (A), others to the middle layer (B) and the remaining ones to the top layer (C). Which alternative shows the mass of the components in decreasing order?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements shows the future promise of biological sciences?
options: Finding alternative living place for human population
Using stem cells to repair damaged organs and grow new organ
Finding the adaptation mechanism of plant in new condition
Advising the government on how to conserve environment
questions.explanation: The use of stem cells to repair or replace damaged tissues and organs represents a cutting-edge and promising application of biological sciences in medicine, highlighting its future potential.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives contains only organic molecules?
options: Glucose, carbon dioxide, glycine and linoleic acid
Methane, calcium carbonate, linoleic acid and glucose
Methane, glycine, linoleic acid and glucose
Linoleic acid, glucose, calcium carbonate and methane
questions.explanation:
Organic molecules contain carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds.

 Methane (CH4), glycine (an amino acid), linoleic acid (a fatty acid), and glucose (a carbohydrate) are all organic molecules. Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) and carbon dioxide (CO2) are inorganic.

questions.questionText: Which one among the following processes occurs during the light independent phase of photosynthesis?
options: Cyclic photophosphorylation of ADP in the thylakoid
Excitation of electrons from chlorophyll molecules
Splitting of water molecules into its components
Reduction of triose molecules by hydrogen from NADPH
questions.explanation: During the light-independent phase (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis, ATP and NADPH produced in the light-dependent reactions are used to reduce 3-carbon molecules (triose phosphates) to form glucose and other carbohydrates.

questions.questionText: As compared to non- cyclic photophosphorylation, the cyclic photophosphorylation uses the
options: photosystem I as the last electron acceptor.
photosystem I to produce ATP and reduced NADP in the stroma.
hydrolysis of water to replace electrons lost from photosystem II.
photosystem II as the first electron donor to NADP.
questions.explanation:
In cyclic photophosphorylation, electrons excited in Photosystem I are cycled back to the same photosystem via the electron transport chain, producing ATP but not NADPH. 

There is no involvement of Photosystem II or water splitting in this process.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following chemical reactions summarizes the process of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation:
Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water in the presence of light energy to produce glucose and oxygen.

 The overall balanced reaction is: 6CO₂ + 12H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements properly describes the structure of ATP? It is made up of
options: one adenine base attached to a pentose sugar and three phosphate groups.
two adenine bases attached to a hexose sugar and three phosphate groups.
two adenine bases attached to a deoxyribose sugar and two phosphate groups.
one adenine base attached to a ribose sugar and two phosphate groups.
questions.explanation:
ATP (adenosine triphosphate) consists of a single adenine base attached to a five-carbon sugar (ribose) and three phosphate groups. 
It serves as the primary energy carrier in cells.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following descriptions about glycolysis is correct? It is a process
options: of producing acetyl CoA from pyruvate by releasing CO2.
that produces a net of 4 ATP through substrate level phosphorylation.
of breaking down of a glucose molecule to two pyruvates.
that takes place in the cytosol with high demand of oxygen.
questions.explanation:
Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway in which one glucose molecule (C₆H₁₂O₆) is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate.

 It occurs in the cytosol, does not require oxygen (anaerobic), and produces a net of 2 ATP molecules per glucose.

questions.questionText: The functional unit of the kidney responsible for filtering blood and forming urine is the:
questions.explanation: The Nephron is the microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney, which consists of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule.

questions.questionText: Why is the skin of a frog important for osmoregulation and respiration?
options: It is covered in thick scales
It is permeable to water and gases
It produces a hard external shell
questions.explanation: A frog's skin is thin and permeable, allowing for the exchange of water and gases, which aids in osmoregulation and cutaneous respiration.

questions.questionText: Farmers want to maintain their sheep with long tails for the next generation through similar sheep from their locality in their breeding program. What process do these farmers apply to keep the desired traits in their program?
questions.explanation:
To maintain a desired trait like long tails in sheep, farmers mate individuals from the same or closely related population that carry the trait. 

This process is called inbreeding, which increases the probability of offspring inheriting the desired characteristics.

questions.questionText:
Four students wanted to conduct chemical tests on unknown food particles and used the following chemicals and materials:

 Student A: Test tubes and biuret solution.

 Student B: Test tubes, ethanol, water, filter paper.

 Student C: Test tubes, benedict's solution, water bath.

 Student D: Test tubes and iodine solution.

 Which of the above students planed a test for lipids?
questions.explanation: "Student B planned the lipid test because the ethanol and water procedure is used in the emulsion test for lipids, where a milky white emulsion indicates the presence of fats.

questions.questionText: Which of the following technological innovations was not explicitly mentioned as being copied from biological nature in the unit's context?
options: Robotic arms from an elephant's trunk
Velcro from the structure of burrs
questions.explanation: The unit mentions robotic arms from an elephant trunk , submarines, flippers, and the bullet train (which is often cited for its nose design imitating a Kingfisher's beak, related to 'flight' and 'submarine' technologies being learned from nature), but not explicitly airplane wings from bird wings, though it is a classic example of biomimicry.

questions.questionText: The development of self-healing materials by scientists, inspired by the way organisms repair their own tissues, is a direct result of which concept?
questions.explanation: Imitating the functional mechanisms of nature, such as tissue repair, to create new materials is the definition of biomimicry.

questions.questionText: The fundamental reason why Biology is essential to the development of Technology is that:
options: Biological research requires complex technological devices.
Technology can only be created by biologists and not engineers.
Biological systems provide a vast reservoir of scientific information and functional designs that can be imitated.
Technology must be tightly blended with biochemistry to be useful.
questions.explanation: The benefits of biology to technology are the biological information and functional principles on biological systems which are helpful to derive technological systems, working mechanisms, and related products.

questions.questionText: Which term refers to the moral rightness or wrongness of using biotechnological information, products, or devices on human health and livelihood systems?
questions.explanation: Bioethics (or Ethical issues in biology) deals with the moral implications and controversies of biological discoveries and their technological applications.

questions.questionText: What does the ethical issue of Immorality in biology encompass?
options: Acts that are against accepted moral, social, or religious principles.
questions.explanation: Immorality is defined as acting against the standards of right and wrong, and the unit lists it alongside unethicality and illegality as a key bioethical concern.

questions.questionText: The negative impact of biotechnology that involves the selling or treating of human body parts as commercial goods is referred to as:
options: Commodification and commercialization of human organs
questions.explanation: Ethical issues in biology include concerns over the commercialization and commodification of human organs, which involves treating body parts as products for sale rather than respected biological entities.

questions.questionText: The hydrogen ions that used to turn the rotor of ATP synthase come from
questions.explanation:
During the electron transport chain, NADH and FADH₂ are oxidized and release electrons.

 The energy released is used to pump hydrogen ions (H⁺) across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

 These hydrogen ions flow back through ATP synthase, turning its rotor and driving ATP production.

questions.questionText: If a scientist studies the internal cooling system of a desert beetle to design a more efficient radiator, the knowledge gained is categorized as:
options: Biological information helpful to derive technological systems
questions.explanation: This falls under the benefits of biology to technology, where biological information (how the beetle cools itself) provides the scientific basis for a technological product (a radiator).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of the economic importance of insects in agriculture and food production? Their role as
questions.explanation: Insects play a critical direct role in agriculture as key plant pollinators for crops and as nutrient-dense food sources (entomophagy) in food production systems.

questions.questionText: Sexual reproduction in animals involves the combination of genetic material from two parents through the process of:
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction is characterized by the involvement of two individual parents to produce offspring by combining genetic materials through fertilization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a key process involved in carbon cycle?
questions.explanation:
The key processes in the carbon cycle include photosynthesis (plants take in CO₂), cellular respiration (release of CO₂ by organisms), and decomposition (release of carbon from dead organisms).
 Evaporation is part of the water cycle, not the carbon cycle.

questions.questionText: Which of the following insect life cycles includes the stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult?
questions.explanation: Complete metamorphosis is a series of major changes in body structure in insects that includes the egg, larva, pupa, and adult stages.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the conservation mechanism of wild life?
options: Indigenous practices relay on the use of taboos for conservation of plants.
Modern practices relay on growing invasive plants in mountainous area in order to prevent soil erosion.
Controlled wildlife hunting areas can't be considered one of the conservation mechanisms.
Wild life conservation is selective protection of a species with economic significances and eliminating less valued species.
questions.explanation: Indigenous conservation strategies traditionally rely on social norms, sacred groves, and cultural taboos to restrict the exploitation of specific plant and animal species.

questions.questionText: Which phylum of invertebrates typically reproduces asexually by fragmentation?
questions.explanation: Fragmentation, where a body part breaks off and regenerates into a whole new organism, is a form of asexual reproduction found in certain invertebrates like starfish.

questions.questionText: A sequence of events that take place in a parent cell as a means of distributing genetic material to form daughter cells is
questions.explanation: The cell cycle is the ordered series of events that leads to cell duplication and division into daughter cells.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an ethical breach related to animal welfare in biological studies?
options: Using the minimal number of animals for a statistically valid result.
Conducting a painful procedure on an animal without administering appropriate anesthesia.
Providing the animals with clean water and food.
Hatching eggs from a bird's nest.
questions.explanation: Failing to minimize pain and suffering, such as by withholding anesthesia for painful procedures, violates the principle of Refinement and is considered unethical.

questions.questionText: What is the primary product of the sexual reproduction process in birds that houses the developing embryo?
questions.explanation: Birds lay an egg, which is the product of internal fertilization and provides the environment for the embryo to develop until hatching.

questions.questionText: In water, phospholipids become organized into a bilayer. In this arrangement, which part of the bilayer faces towards the water?
questions.explanation: The phosphate head of a phospholipid is hydrophilic (water-loving) and faces the aqueous environment both inside and outside the cell.

questions.questionText: Suppose there was a cross between pea plants with flower positions axial (AA) and terminal (aa) and produced F1 generation. What will be the most probable number of heterozygous dominant individuals obtained if 1000 offspring were produced by self-crossing of F1 generation?
questions.explanation:
F1 generation (Aa) self-cross gives a genotypic ratio of 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa.

 Among 1000 offspring, 2/4 are heterozygous dominant (Aa), which equals 500 individuals.

questions.questionText: In which animal group is asexual reproduction by fragmentation and regeneration most likely to occur?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction, including fragmentation, is more common among invertebrates than in vertebrates.

questions.questionText: Why is **Nature** described as a 'reliable source of knowledgeable ideas'?
options: Because natural systems have been optimized and tested by evolution over vast timescales.
Because nature is always changing randomly.
Because nature is completely inaccessible to human study.
Because only inanimate objects exist in nature.
questions.explanation: The unit's review questions assert that 'Nature is a reliable source of knowledgeable ideas', which is true because its designs are evolutionary 'success stories' and thus excellent models for engineering.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the action of apoenzymes and coenzymes?
options: Coenzymes bind with enzymes to give catalytic activity.
Both apoenzymes and coenzymes combine with cofactors to form a non-active enzyme.
Apoenzymes bind with enzymes to give catalytic activity.
Coenzymes bind with cofactors to form an active enzyme.
questions.explanation:
An apoenzyme (inactive protein part) combined with a coenzyme (organic cofactor) forms a holoenzyme (active enzyme).

 Option A correctly states that coenzymes bind with enzymes (apoenzymes) to enable catalytic activity.

questions.questionText: The use of MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) to non-invasively view soft tissue structures in the human body is categorized as a use of technology in biology/medicine because it:
options: Aids in the investigation and diagnosis of biological conditions.
questions.explanation: MRI is an advanced imaging technology that provides detailed biological information for diagnosis, fitting the description of a technological application in biology.

questions.questionText: If an insect's young stage (nymph) looks like a small version of the adult and lacks a pupal stage, its development is known as:
questions.explanation: Incomplete metamorphosis is defined by the absence of a pupal stage and the young (nymphs) resembling the adults, only smaller and sexually immature.

questions.questionText: Why is the invention of the vaccine considered a major positive impact of biology on society?
options: It has significantly reduced the incidence and mortality of many infectious diseases.
It has caused more pollution than industrial factories.
questions.explanation: The discovery and use of vaccines, a biological product, has had one of the most profound positive impacts on public health and increased human life expectancy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes how enzymes speed up the rate of chemical reactions? By
options: lowering the energy of reactants required to react more easily
decreasing the collision between substrate and enzyme
increasing the concentrations of reactants and speeding the reaction
being part of the reactants and product in a reaction
questions.explanation: Enzymes act as biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions by lowering the activation energy required for the reactants to reach the transition state.

questions.questionText: An animal repeatedly exposed to a harmless stimulus eventually stops responding to it. This learned behavior is called:
questions.explanation: Habituation is a type of learning where an animal decreases its response to a repeated, harmless stimulus.

questions.questionText: When three fatty acid molecules and a glycerol molecule undergo condensation reaction, they form
questions.explanation:
The reaction between three fatty acids and one glycerol molecule forms a triglyceride and three molecules of water.

 The bond connecting the fatty acids to the glycerol is an ester bond.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a primary negative consequence associated with the release of Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) into the natural environment?
options: Potential loss of genetic purity in wild relatives through cross-pollination.
questions.explanation: A major concern with GMOs is the potential for gene flow to wild populations, which can lead to the loss of genetic diversity and purity in natural ecosystems, a significant negative environmental impact.

questions.questionText: The control of water and electrolyte levels in the body is managed by osmoregulation through mechanisms such as:
questions.explanation: Urine production by the kidney and the sensation of thirst are key mechanisms by which the body regulates water and electrolyte balance.

questions.questionText: How does a competitive inhibitor affect an enzyme catalyzed reaction? By
options: blocking the allosteric site of the enzyme.
blocking the active site of the enzyme.
denaturing the active site of the enzyme.
producing conformational change of the enzyme.
questions.explanation:
A competitive inhibitor is a molecule that is structurally similar to the substrate.
 It competes directly with the substrate for binding to the enzyme's active site. 

By binding to the active site, it prevents the actual substrate from binding, thus blocking the active site of the enzyme and reducing the reaction rate.

questions.questionText: The process of synthesizing RNA from a DNA template is called:
questions.explanation: Transcription is the process where a segment of DNA is copied into RNA (messenger RNA) by the enzyme RNA polymerase.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following causes of infertility in female when she decided not to have any more children?
questions.explanation: Voluntary sterilization (such as tubal ligation) is a permanent surgical method chosen by individuals who do not wish to have any more children.

questions.questionText: Which animal group produces offspring that develop in the uterus and are nourished via a placenta?
questions.explanation: Mammals, such as the rat, are characterized by internal embryonic development within the female's uterus, often supported by a placenta.

questions.questionText: Which invertebrate group includes animals with jointed legs and an exoskeleton, such as insects?
questions.explanation: Insects are part of the phylum Arthropoda, which is characterized by segmented bodies, jointed appendages, and an exoskeleton.

questions.questionText: If a red snapdragon flower (RR) is crossed with a white snapdragon flower (rr), and the resulting F1 generation is all pink (Rr), this is an example of:
questions.explanation: In Incomplete dominance, the heterozygous phenotype is intermediate between the two homozygous phenotypes (blending effect, e.g., pink).

questions.questionText: What is the primary role of the enzyme lactase in the dairy industry?
questions.explanation:
Lactase hydrolyzes lactose (the milk sugar) into glucose and galactose.
 This is used to produce lactose-free milk for people who are lactose intolerant, making it easier to digest.

questions.questionText: Industries in the medicine sector use glucose oxidase in Clinistix strips for
options: easy diagnosis of diabetes by examining a urine sample.
restoring blood supply to areas of heart muscle.
detecting toxic metabolites in the blood.
questions.explanation:
Glucose oxidase is an enzyme used in Clinistix strips to detect glucose in urine.

 High glucose levels in urine indicate hyperglycemia, which helps in the diagnosis of diabetes.

questions.questionText: How does increasing the concentration of a competitive inhibitor affect the enzyme reaction rate in the short term?
options: It causes an immediate decrease in the reaction rate.
It shifts the enzyme's optimum pH.
It increases the enzyme's substrate specificity.
questions.explanation:
A competitive inhibitor directly competes with the substrate for the active site.
 Increasing its concentration will increase the proportion of enzyme molecules bound to the inhibitor, thus immediately reducing the number of free active sites available for the substrate, leading to a decrease in the reaction rate.

questions.questionText: What is the effect of doubling the concentration of a competitive inhibitor in a fixed-enzyme, fixed-substrate system?
options: The proportion of inhibited enzyme decreases.
The proportion of enzyme bound to the inhibitor increases.
questions.explanation:
Increasing the concentration of a competitive inhibitor increases its chance of binding to the active site, thereby increasing the proportion of inhibited enzyme.

 Kinetically, competitive inhibition increases the apparent Km (lowers the apparent affinity) but does not change Vmax.

questions.questionText: What is the key difference between resource exploitation and sustainable resource utilization?
options: Exploitation focuses on non-renewable resources, while utilization focuses on renewable ones.
Exploitation occurs only in developing nations, while utilization occurs only in developed nations.
Exploitation maximizes immediate profit without regard for future availability; utilization manages use for long-term supply.
Exploitation involves local use, while utilization involves global trade of resources.
questions.explanation: Exploitation prioritizes short-term gain (often leading to depletion), whereas sustainable utilization seeks to manage the resource so that it remains available for future generations.

questions.questionText: The enzymatic cleavage of lactose into glucose and galactose is catalyzed by which class of enzyme?
questions.explanation: The enzyme lactase (or beta-galactosidase) breaks the glycosidic bond in lactose by adding a water molecule (hydrolysis), which places it in the Hydrolase class.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the best definition of Biotechnology according to the unit's context?
options: The use of biology to develop new products, methods, and organisms intended to improve human health and society.
The study of living organisms from the simplest to the most complex ones.
The sum of techniques, skills, and processes used in the production of goods or services.
The imitation of engineering systems from the structures of inanimate objects.
questions.explanation: Biotechnology is defined as the use of biological systems or living organisms and derivatives thereof, to make or modify products or processes for a specific use, as stated in the unit summary.

questions.questionText: In protein synthesis, the anticodon is found on which molecule?
questions.explanation: The anticodon is the three-base sequence on the tRNA (transfer RNA) that is complementary to the codon on the mRNA, ensuring the correct amino acid is delivered.

questions.questionText: What is the name for the inactive precursor form of a proteolytic enzyme that is stored in the pancreas to prevent self-digestion?
questions.explanation:
Digestive enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin are synthesized and stored as inactive zymogens (proenzymes), such as trypsinogen and chymotrypsinogen, respectively, to prevent the enzymes from breaking down the cells that produce them.

 They are activated only after secretion into the small intestine.

questions.questionText: In the industrial application of biological detergents, what is the main function of the enzyme lipase?
options: Breaking down fat and oil stains.
questions.explanation:
Lipases are hydrolases that break down lipids (fats and oils) into glycerol and fatty acids.

 This makes them highly effective in biological detergents for removing greasy stains.

questions.questionText: The function of a kinase enzyme in metabolism is to catalyze the transfer of:
questions.explanation:
Kinases are a type of Transferase enzyme that specifically catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group** from a high-energy phosphate donor molecule, such as ATP, to a substrate.

 This is a crucial step in regulating many metabolic pathways.

questions.questionText:
The following are reaction types catalyzed by different classes of enzymes:

 1. Transferring hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

 2. Changing of the molecular form of the substrate.

 3. Joining of two molecules by the formation of new bonds.

 Which classes of enzymes catalyze the above reactions according to their consecutive order?
questions.explanation:
1. Transferring H and O: Oxidoreductases (involved in redox).

2. Changing molecular form: Isomerases (rearrange atoms). 

3. Joining two molecules: Ligases (form new bonds using ATP).

questions.questionText: An organic molecule which is an important part of structure of chromosome is
questions.explanation:
Chromosomes are primarily composed of DNA and proteins (histones).

 Proteins are polymers made up of amino acids. Amylose and glycogen are carbohydrates, and triglyceride is a lipid.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would be considered a potential negative impact of technology on the natural world?
options: Improvement of crop yields through genetically modified organisms (GMOs).
Increased pollution and resource depletion from manufacturing processes.
Improved early disease detection using advanced scanning devices.
questions.explanation:
The impacts of biology and technology include both positive and negative influences.
 While technology offers benefits like improved health, its rapid industrial development can lead to negative environmental consequences such as pollution and resource depletion.

questions.questionText: The process of using a template strand of DNA to make an RNA molecule is catalyzed by:
questions.explanation: RNA Polymerase is the enzyme responsible for synthesizing RNA by reading the template strand of the DNA molecule.

questions.questionText: In the context of the relationship between science and technology, Technology is described as:
options: The physical, natural, and material world of life.
The use or application of scientific knowledge for a specific goal or purpose.
The natural science studying living organisms.
questions.explanation: Technology is the use or application of scientific knowledge for a specific goal or purpose.

questions.questionText: In DNA, Guanine (G) always pairs with which base?
questions.explanation: According to Chargaff's rules and the structure of DNA, Guanine (G) always pairs with Cytosine (C) via three hydrogen bonds.

questions.questionText: Which process explains the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes during Prophase I of meiosis, creating new combinations of alleles?
questions.explanation: Crossing over (or genetic recombination) is the physical exchange of chromosome segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, increasing genetic variation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered the most fundamental benefit of biology to technology?
options: Biology provides the raw materials (like wood and cotton) for technology.
Biology offers scientific information, principles, and successful designs that can be applied to engineering.
Biology regulates the ethical use of technology.
questions.explanation: The primary benefit is that biological information on biological systems is helpful to derive technological systems and working mechanisms.

questions.questionText: In asexual reproduction, offspring are generally:
options: Genetically identical to the single parent
Genetically different from the single parent
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction involves a single individual, and the offspring are typically genetically identical clones of the parent.

questions.questionText: In a test cross, the genotype of unknown organism cross with
questions.explanation: A test cross involves breeding an individual showing a dominant phenotype (whose exact genotype is unknown) with an individual expressing the homozygous recessive genotype to determine whether the first organism is homozygous or heterozygous.

questions.questionText: The use of remote sensing satellites in biology to monitor deforestation or vegetation health is an example of:
questions.explanation: Remote sensing is a technological application used to gather environmental data for biological and ecological studies.

questions.questionText: If a bird's body temperature is consistently maintained at 40 degrees Celsius, regardless of the air temperature, it is a:
questions.explanation: Birds are homeothermic animals, which means they maintain a constant internal body temperature independent of the environment.

questions.questionText: A dog learning to salivate at the sound of a bell after being consistently fed when the bell rings is an example of which type of behavior?
questions.explanation: Learned or acquired behavior is modified by experience. [cite_start]The dog has acquired the association between the bell and food, which is not an inherent trait.

questions.questionText: In allosteric regulation, a positive allosteric effector (activator) binds to the allosteric site and causes a conformational change that:
options: Decreases the enzyme's affinity for the substrate.
Competes with the substrate for the active site.
questions.explanation: A positive allosteric effector (activator) binds to the allosteric site and stabilizes the active (high-affinity) conformation of the enzyme, thereby increasing its catalytic activity and, often, its apparent affinity for the substrate, leading to a higher Vmax.

questions.questionText: Niacin is used to make the coenzyme
questions.explanation: Niacin (vitamin B3) is a precursor used to synthesize the coenzyme NAD (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide), which functions in oxidation–reduction reactions in cells.

questions.questionText: An animal displaying 'fight or flight' response when faced with danger is primarily exhibiting:
questions.explanation: The 'fight or flight' response is a stress-induced, inherent physiological and behavioral reaction to a perceived threat.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about transport of substances across the cell membrane?
options: Facilitated diffusion - particles move from high water potential to lower one.
Simple diffusion - large particles transported through channel proteins .
Active transport - particles move from low to higher concentration using carrier protein .
Passive transport - particles require energy in the form of ATP to derive the transport.
questions.explanation:
Active transport requires energy (ATP) to move substances against their concentration gradient, meaning from a region of low to high concentration, typically utilizing specialized protein carriers (pumps). Option A describes osmosis.

 Option B is partially true, but facilitated diffusion is for movement down the concentration gradient.

questions.questionText: Which technological device is primarily used to gather geographical data or information in the context of ecological studies?
questions.explanation: The Global Positioning System (GPS) is a technological device that uses satellites to determine exact locations and collect geographical data, which is useful in field biology and ecological studies.
